facts: k11-13a:A student gets an email saying their school account will be closed unless they f
text:
A student gets an email saying their school account will be closed unless they follow a link and type in their password. The address looks almost right, but has one wrong letter.
(i) What kind of attack is this? [1]
(ii) What’s one sign that it’s fake? [1]
(iii) What should the student do? [1]

points.text: (i) Phishing.
(ii) The sender’s address is slightly wrong, or the message is pressing for urgent action.
(iii) Not click the link, and report the message to the school.

text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) malware
(2) plagiarism
(3) cloud computing
(4) phishing
Column B
(a) Using someone else’s work, and passing it off as your own.
(b) Using computing services over the internet, rather than on your own machine.
(c) Software designed to harm a computer or steal from it.
(d) Tricking people into giving away personal information, usually with a fake message or website.

points.text: (1) malware goes with (c).
(2) plagiarism goes with (a).
(3) cloud computing goes with (b).
(4) phishing goes with (d).
